scope: Verified native player control-state bytes and nearest world-ray query. Evidence is excluded from website output; no native binaries are included.

inventoryReview.reason: The full preview includes unrelated sibling-project work. Adopted only exact scanner records and their source snapshots for the task symbols; preserved all existing inventoried symbols.
inventoryReview.updatedExistingSource: All existing symbol references/declarations from the changed anchor_player_models.c snapshot were refreshed together, preserving unrelated source references.

nativeEvidence.finding: MIPS lbu at absolute 0x800C7AE0, andi 3, nonzero branch bypasses calls 0x801CC4C0/0x801CD084/0x801CBBE8. Native common.h confirms full g_system base 0x8008CCC0 and u8 offset +0x3AE20.
Native special-action input handler separately checks bit 4. The late collision handler does not use bit 4 as its bypass.

Move-toward helper loads byte at absolute 0x800C7AE3, ORs 1, stores byte, supplies synthetic stick magnitude/direction at player input offsets. Eocs creation sets byte=1; playback callback holds=1 until completion then clears byte=0 and selected player work input word before task deletion.

Reviewed decompilation/disassembly: output pointer followed by seven floats; 0x48 byte output copy and same output pointer returned; static and mode-1 dynamic queries choose nearest squared distance. Downward wrapper establishes normalized direction (0,-1,0) and float distance. Native shadow positioning adds result displacement +0x18/+0x1C/+0x20 to ray origin; normal +0x24/+0x28/+0x2C; u16 hit +0x38=0x7FFF; float distance squared +0x3C; dynamic collision pointers +0x40/+0x44.

Dynamic ray mode initializes nearest squared distance to float2000 via LUI0x44FA/MTC1f20 independently of requested range; candidate return is the XYZ hit-displacement squared norm from800273E0. Strict nearest comparison can omit dynamic hits beyondsqrt2000. Use normalized nonzero rays in short segments32.

Player constructor LHU reads charIndex*2 table entries,SH writes task+3C/+3E. Native body-contact helper reads both fields unsigned16 and multiplies radius by object scaleX and height by scaleY. This registers contact hits, not solid movement resolution.

scalarReads.note: Both local decompressed images returned these same eight halfwords; no binary content beyond the scalar values is included.

nativeEvidence.finding: Native post callback takes task inA0 and savesA1 secondcallbackarg but doesnotuseit. Tests work+69 before helper801DABDC; &3 controlbits skip worldcollision/contactblock; transformmaintenance andcontactclear stillfollow. Entrypoint/return hooks bracket native processing.
Dynamic radial routine supplies radius+2 to800322A8; helper invokes80032320 mode1 with suppliedrange+2. Shared2000nearest-squareddistance caveat applies tolargeworldradiusspokes aswell.

Ghidra analysis against the US decompressed ROM (SHA256 e40bee20508c2e29e651dca4e47504e40f908f0a2186e34a582784bf5a64be4c) establishes func_801CEEA8_58ADB8 ABI (player task, mutable float[3] output delta, const float[3] proposed delta) -> u16. Its sole caller is func_801CC4C0_5883D0 at 0x801CC9FC; its downward func_8002C9D4_2D5D4 ray at 0x801CF118 starts at proposed feet Y +2.1 and only selects/adjusts floor height. It does not set DAT_8020CA66 or work+0x0A bit 0x10. It can miss a floor crossed by more than 2.1 world units in one tick. Actual grounded contact is handled by func_801D0C64_58CB74, called twice by func_801CFE24_58BD34. Its ABI is task A0, primary object A1, mutable proposed world position A2, movement vector A3, sample-offset buffer stack argument 5 and direction vector stack argument 6. Its downward ray at 0x801D0F7C starts at proposed feet plus normally 185 times player scale. On an accepted upward-normal hit, it sets work+0x0A bit 0x10 at 0x801D1004, adjusts proposed feet to ray origin plus hit delta Y at 0x801D1018-0x801D1040, and stores ground-plane/point state. It writes DAT_8020CA66 from record surface halfword +0x36, or 1 when that halfword is zero, at 0x801D11E0-0x801D1200; the later caller arrests downward velocity. func_801D1358_58D268 takes task, primary display object, mutable proposed delta, opaque argument, sample-offset buffer as argument 5 and direction vector as argument 6. func_801CFE24_58BD34 calls it twice; its upward ray at 0x801D1520 tests head contact. On an accepted hit it sets work+0x0A bit 0x100, adjusts proposed XYZ and clears a positive task float+0xA4.

The world-ray query ABI is (out, x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, range); the final four float arguments are stack-passed in the MIPS caller. Its 0x48-byte output stores displacement at +0x18/+0x1C/+0x20, normal at +0x24/+0x28/+0x2C, hit at +0x38, squared distance at +0x3C, and dynamic object/task pointers at +0x40/+0x44. Dynamic results come from registered actor lists and resource slots; arbitrary display-list Gfx is not collision registration.

US decompressed ROM resource file 0x191 spans 0x0103F1C0..0x010401D0. Its direct display list at file offset 0x500 loads 24 vertices from segment 8 +0x380. Signed XYZ vertex extrema are -50..+50. This records render geometry only; it does not prove that an arbitrary visible Gfx object has been registered with dynamic collision.

wallCorrectionEvidence.finding: Five floats after output pointer, low/high absolute Y.24 radial queries. Hit requires distance squared <= radius squared and normal.y <0.5; preserve nearest metadata; accumulates opposing X/Z corrections; output 72 bytes; hit+0x38 gates valid correction at +0x18/+0x20, deltaY+0x1C zero. Static uses8002AA00; dynamic uses800322A8.

limitations: No two-client native runtime validation was performed for these findings.
D_800C7AE3 is scoped to inspected native scripted-input paths; it does not claim every cinematic has this state.
Ray output fields +0x30..+0x37 and +0x3A..+0x3B remain opaque; a ray is not a swept volume.
The vertex bounds describe the file 0x191 display-list mesh; they are not proof of the registered dynamic collision shape or a complete swept-player collision volume.
